title: Account keeps locking out
symptom: User's account locks again shortly after every unlock, even though she types the right password
user_description: This is the third day in a row. You unlock me, I sign in fine, then an hour later I'm locked out again. I changed my password last week, I'm typing it right!

options.text: Turn off account lockout for her account
options.why: This removes protection against password guessing and leaves the real cause in place.

options.text: Give her a password that never expires
options.why: It does not fix the lockouts and weakens security.

options.text: Unlock her account every morning when she calls
options.why: This wastes time every day and never finds the cause.

options.text: Find the source: lockout events on the domain controller (event 4740) show which computer caused it. Usually an old password is still saved on her phone, in Credential Manager, a mapped drive or a service, so update or remove it
options.why: Something keeps trying her old password and triggers the lockout. Finding and updating it stops the lockouts for good.

hints: What changed just before this started?
Where else might her old password still be saved?
Can the server tell you which device is causing the lockout?
real_world_tip: Phones syncing work email are the most common cause after a password change. Ask the user to update the password on every device they use.
